To facilitate this we employ dimensional regularization and BPHZ renormalization to compute the 1-loop contribution to the graviton self-energy, in pure quantum gravity, on de Sitter background, in the simplest gauge. We then solve the effective field equations to derive 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, and to the Newtonian potential. Although it seems possible to renormalize in such a way that the mode function shows no secular growth, the Newtonian potential grows like the third power of the number of e-foldings.
item.dc:creator: B. Yesilyurt (U. Florida), N. C. Tsamis (U. Crete), R. P. Woodard (U. Florida)

item.title: Detection times are not local observables in quantum field theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.02135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Detection times are routinely recorded in quantum experiments. We show that, under natural covariance and consistency requirements, the observables describing these times cannot be algebraically localized in any bounded spacetime region, even when the records themselves are localized. This challenges the identification of algebraic localization with the physical localization of measurements and shows why microcausality alone does not establish non-signalling for measurements in quantum field theory.
item.dc:creator: Charis Anastopoulos, Ntina Savvidou

item.title: Projective relativistic dynamics from a quantum Lorentz algebra: time-dependent deformed Hamiltonians on (anti-)de Sitter spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A (non-standard) quantum deformation of the Lorentz algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ is used to construct novel time-dependent Hamiltonian systems on the (anti-)de Sitter spacetimes in $(1+1)$-dimensions. The specific deformation considered here contains, among others, the non-standard quantum deformation of $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{R})$ and that of the `book' algebra $\mathfrak{b}_{2}$ as quantum subalgebras. The guiding idea is to apply the theory of Poisson--Hopf deformations of Lie--Hamilton systems to the Lorentz deformation, giving rise to a broad family of time-dependent deformed systems that share the same deformed Poisson--Hopf Lorentz algebra symmetry. In particular, this approach provides Hamiltonian vector fields expressed in terms of certain projective canonical variables, which, in turn, are related to the usual Beltrami variables via a canonical transformation. Under this construction, it is shown that the underlying Lorentizan spaces possess constant curvature $\kappa$ and the quantum deformation parameter $z$ can be identified with $\kappa$, such that the cosmological constant is $\Lambda=-z\equiv -\kappa$. Therefore, we deal with the anti-de Sitter, de Sitter and Minkowskian spaces for $z>0$, $z<0$ and $z=0$ (the undeformed case), respectively. Finally, as applications, we study time-dependent deformed oscillators on the (anti-)de Sitter spaces in detail, as well as time-dependent deformed Bateman and generalised coupled Caldirola--Kanai Hamiltonians.
item.dc:creator: Rutwig Campoamor-Stursberg, Oscar Carballal, Francisco J. Herranz

item.title: Static Vacuum Geometry Encodes Gravitational Collapse and Cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2611.02358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, within covariant Hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, a prescribed one-parameter family of static vacuum geometries uniquely determines the local dynamics of gravitational collapse coupled to irrotational dust, despite the nonuniqueness of the underlying gravitational Hamiltonian. We further derive necessary and sufficient conditions under which the resulting dynamics admits a homogeneous and isotropic cosmological sector. These conditions establish a two-way correspondence between static vacuum geometries and modified Friedmann dynamics and impose a universal restriction on the spatial-curvature dependence of the latter. Our results provide a criterion for determining whether independently proposed black-hole and cosmological models can arise from a common covariant gravitational theory.
item.dc:creator: Yi Ling, Jinsong Yang, Zhangping Yu, Cong Zhang

item.title: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
item.description: arXiv:2611.02417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.
item.dc:creator: Peter Koroteev

item.title: 2+1 flavor light hadron spectrum with PACS10 configurations
item.description: arXiv:2611.02426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the results for the hadron spectrum, the pseudoscalar meson decay constants, and the quark mass ratio in the continuum limit using the ``PACS10'' gauge configurations generated with the $O(a)$-improved Wilson quark action and the Iwasaki gauge action. Numerical simulations are carried out at three lattice spacings keeping the space-time volumes over (10 fm$)^4$ in 2+1 flavor QCD at the physical point. We calculate physical quantities with two choices of conventions to define pseudoexperimental values expected in the isosymmetric QCD. In order to investigate the finite size effects on the physical quantities we have additionally generated the (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice at the coarsest lattice spacing of $a=0.08487(14)$~fm, which is a hypercube with half the length in each direction compared to the PACS10 configurations. While the finite size effect is hardly observed in comparison of the hadron effective masses on the (10.9 fm$)^4$ and (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattices, the results for the pseudoscalar meson decay constants show discrepancies beyond the error bars. The (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice also serves for determining the expansion parameters of the pseudoscalar meson masses and decay constants, and the octet baryon masses in terms of the quark masses around the physical point with the aid of the mass reweighting technique. The expansion parameters are used for the fine-tuning of the physical point employing the pseudoexperimental masses of the $\pi$ meson, $K$ meson, and the $\Xi$ baryon as physical inputs in each convention. We compare the results for the octet baryon masses and the pseudoscalar decay constants in the continuum limit with the corresponding pseudoexperimental values in both conventions. We also discuss the deviation between two results with different conventions. As for the quark mass ratio the result is compared with the recent FLAG summary.

item.title: A simple flux criterion for trapped surface formation by short pulses of gravitational radiation and matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.02569v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We discuss the formation of trapped surfaces induced by short pulses of incoming gravitational radiation and matter fields, in a double-null formulation. We identify a hierarchy of orders in the pulse width for the geometric and matter quantities consistent with the evolution equations. Under the assumption that this hierarchy holds throughout the region considered, the incoming fluxes undergo approximately conservative inward transport and are thereby amplified. The Raychaudhuri equation then gives an initial flux criterion for trapped surface formation. The conditions on the matter are expressed through the Ricci components and their derivatives, which allows the argument to be developed without specifying a particular matter model.
item.dc:creator: Tetsuya Shiromizu, Keisuke Izumi, Daisuke Yoshida

item.title: Cloudy black-hole configurations of the composed Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory: Analytic treatment
item.description: arXiv:2611.02656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-Abelian black holes that violate the non-hair conjecture are known to exist in the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory. The onset of hair formation in this composed physical system is marked by the presence of `cloudy' black-hole spacetimes, magnetically charged Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes that support spatially regular linearized field configurations. In the present paper we explore, using {\it analytical} techniques, the physical and mathematical properties of the composed black-hole-linearized-field bound-state configurations of the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs theory. In particular, we derive a remarkably compact analytical formula for the discrete resonance spectrum $\{\mu_k\}^{k=\infty}_{k=1}$ of the dimensionless mass-radius parameter $\mu\equiv m_{\text{w}} r_+$ that characterizes the cloudy black-hole-field configurations in the regime $1\ll r_+\ll m^{-1}_{\text{w}}$ of small-mass weakly-magnetized black holes (here $r_+$ is the horizon radius of the central supporting black hole and $m_{\text{w}}$ is the mass of the Yang-Mills field due to the Higgs effect). Interestingly, our results reveal that the excited black-hole-field resonances are characterized by the asymptotic $k$-independent dimensionless ratio ${{\mu_{k+1}}/{\mu_{k}}}=e^{-{{2\pi}/{\sqrt{3}}}}$.
item.dc:creator: Shahar Hod

item.title: Universal Curve Counting in Calabi-Yau 4-folds
item.description: arXiv:2611.02717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, Pardon introduced a universal curve counting framework, which allows him to show that curve counting on 3-folds is "generated" by local curves (in a precise sense). We implement this universal curve counting program for Calabi-Yau 4-folds, where a significant technical difficulty comes from the dependence of the virtual dimension on the genus, which leads to more complicated generators than just local curves. Our main techniques are combinations of deformation-theoretic and homotopy-theoretic methods with an adaptation of Pardon's generic transversality results, which allow us to establish a full set of (computable) generators for CY4 curve counting. As a result, we prove (a slight correction of) the Gromov-Witten/Pandharipande-Thomas correspondence with primary descendents for CY4-folds, formulated by Cao, Maulik, and Toda. From this, we additionally obtain integrality of Gopakumar-Vafa style invariants for CY4-folds, as conjectured by Klemm-Pandharipande.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Karpov, Felix Thimm

item.title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.02841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.
item.dc:creator: M. Cristina Diamantini, Carlo A. Trugenberger

item.title: Spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: Stabilizing the unstable
item.description: arXiv:2611.03070v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. Small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. We study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on Reissner--Nordstr\"om and Reissner--Nordstr\"om--de Sitter backgrounds. A localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. In the asymptotically flat case, a quasinormal branch enters the superradiant frequency regime while remaining damped. By searching for competing modes, we show that the least-damped positive-frequency mode also enters this regime, after a series of mode overtakings driven by quasinormal-mode migration. The real-frequency amplification, nevertheless, is only weakly affected and develops no pronounced narrow resonance. In de Sitter black holes, the bump can move an initially growing monopole mode into the damped half of the complex plane, stabilizing selected configurations that are initially modally unstable. After stabilization, the peak superradiant amplification can remain above both its unperturbed value and a gain of $100\%$; it falls below $100\%$ only for more distant bump locations. A prescribed positive perturbation can thus suppress modal growth without changing the superradiant frequency bounds or immediately suppressing the scattering peak.
item.dc:creator: Kyriakos Destounis

item.title: Second-order evolution of spin shear tensor for massive spin-1/2 particles
item.description: arXiv:2611.03086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the second-order evolution equation for the spin shear component of the spin tensor in spin-polarized fluids, using a classical description of the spin degrees of freedom. Employing a semi-classical kinetic theory for the massive spin-1/2 particles within the relaxation time approximation we obtain a relaxation-type equation describing the evolution of spin shear driven by various thermodynamic forces and high-order gradient corrections. This equation yields a new set of transport coefficients that govern the dynamics of the dissipative spin-shear tensor.
item.dc:creator: Pushpa Panday, Samapan Bhadury, Sadhana Dash

item.title: Enforced Gaplessness by Combining Non-Anomalous Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2611.03164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetry-enforced gaplessness is a phenomenon in which a quantum system is forced to be gapless due to its global symmetry. Previous works have mainly focused on anomalous symmetries. Another approach, using symmetry spans, which specify two embeddings of a common symmetry into two larger symmetries, was proposed by the authors. In this work, we show that a symmetry span can enforce gaplessness even when both larger symmetries are invertible and non-anomalous: each alone admits a trivially gapped phase, but because the embeddings differ by a twist associated with a symmetry-protected topological phase, the symmetry they generate admits no gapped phase with finitely many ground states. We present such a span of a finite group and $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$ in 1+1 dimensions, with continuum realizations and a lattice Hamiltonian, with a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space and finitely many parameters, that is gapless in any region of its parameter space. We also discuss a 2+1-dimensional example and spans of only finite symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Takamasa Ando, Kantaro Ohmori

item.title: The quantum magic of top quarks
item.description: arXiv:2611.03211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.
item.dc:creator: Chris D. White

item.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
item.description: arXiv:2611.03221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $\chi = 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $\tau = 1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
item.dc:creator: Alfie Jones

item.title: Exact Regular Planar Black Holes solutions in Bumblebee gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.03338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We discuss possibilities of finding exact regular planar black hole solutions in bumblebee gravity with temporal and radial components of the bumblebee field. We consider quadratic and linear potentials, with vanishing and nonzero cosmological constants, respectively. The field equations determine the nonminimal coupling and the relations between the model parameters. Found solution produce regular planar black hole with planar deformation function. Analytical expressions for this functions has been found. This solutions free of singularities at the $r=0$.
item.dc:creator: Daniil Stepanenko

item.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.03429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.
item.dc:creator: Samuel S\'anchez L\'opez, Eemeli Tomberg, Juan C. Bueno S\'anchez

item.title: Cherenkov radiation constraint on the photon mass from a two-form gauge potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.03488v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate how electromagnetic radiation in massive antisymmetric tensor theories can be used to constrain the photon mass. In this context, massive electrodynamics constitutes one realization of the $B \wedge F$ class of models in $(3+1)$ dimensions and is obtained by dualizing Stueckelberg-like massive gauge theories. Notably, this model is characterized by the mixing of a $U(1)$ gauge potential with an Abelian $3$-form field of the type found in the topological sector of QCD. We then examine how mass affects permittivity and susceptibility and, consequently, modifies the refractive index through the dispersion relation. We subsequently investigate the electromagnetic radiation emitted by a moving charged particle as it interacts with a medium within the framework of massive electrodynamics. Our findings indicate that the medium through which the particle travels drives the radiation, in a manner analogous to the Cherenkov effect. Applying our results to data on Cherenkov radiation produced at Super-Kamiokande, we derive a photon mass bound of 1 eV ($ 10^ {- 36} $ kg), which is consistent with known estimates based on superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Patricio Gaete, Jos\'{e} Helay\"{e}l-Neto

item.title: Exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
item.description: arXiv:2611.03511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The static interaction potential of two non-spinning point masses in general relativity was previously computed through seventh post-Newtonian order using methods of effective field theory. Its probe limit, or zeroth-self-force contribution, is determined exactly by the Schwarzschild geometry. We derive a closed-form expression for the static first-self-force correction, quadratic in the light mass, and establish its weak-field expansion to all orders. Working in harmonic gauge, we construct the required Green function for the coupled linearised gravitational equations about the Schwarzschild background. We fix its homogeneous contributions and regularised coincident limit by matching to the dimensionally continued point-source theory. The result reproduces known perturbative coefficients and determines all higher static post-Newtonian coefficients in this mass sector.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Monteiro

item.title: A Fresh Look at the Calculation of Tunneling Actions including Gravitational Effects
item.description: arXiv:1808.00420v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, the calculation of tunneling actions, that control the exponential suppression of the decay of metastable vacua, has been reformulated as an elementary variational problem in field space. This paper extends this formalism to include the effect of gravity. Considering tunneling potentials $V_t(\phi)$ that go from the false vacuum $\phi_+$ to some $\phi_0$ on the stable basin of the scalar potential $V(\phi)$, the tunneling action is the minimum of the functional $S_E[V_t]=6 \pi^2m_P^4\int_{\phi_+}^{\phi_0}(D+V_t')^2/(V_t^2D)d\phi $, where $D\equiv [(V_t')^2+6(V-V_t)V_t/m_P^2]^{1/2}$, $V_t'=dV_t/d\phi$ and $m_P$ is the reduced Planck mass. This one-line simple result applies equally to AdS, Minkowski or dS vacua decays and reproduces the Hawking-Moss action in the appropriate cases. This formalism provides new handles for the theoretical understanding of different features of vacuum decay in the presence of gravity.
item.dc:creator: J. R. Espinosa

item.title: Large N instantons, BPS states, and the replica limit
item.description: arXiv:2403.14462v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the relation between large N instantons and conventional instantons, focusing on matrix models and topological strings. We show that the resurgent properties of the perturbative series at fixed but arbitrary N, including the replica limit N = 0, can be obtained from large N instantons. In the case of topological strings, it has been conjectured that the resurgent structure encoded by large N instantons is closely related to the spectrum of BPS states. We give direct evidence for this connection in the case of Seiberg-Witten theory and other topological string models, and we show in detail how the resurgent properties at fixed N follow from the large N theory, and therefore can be used to obtain information on BPS invariants.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Marino, Maximilian Schwick

item.title: New horizons for inhomogeneous quenches and Floquet CFT
item.description: arXiv:2404.07884v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A fruitful avenue in investigating out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is to abruptly change their Hamiltonian and study the subsequent evolution of their quantum state. If this is done once, the setup is called a quench, while if it is done periodically, it is called Floquet driving. We consider the solvable setup of a two-dimensional CFT driven by Hamiltonians built out of conformal symmetry generators: in this case, the quantum dynamics can be understood using two-dimensional geometry. We investigate how the dynamics is reflected in the holographic dual three-dimensional spacetime and find new horizons. We argue that bulk operators behind the new horizons are reconstructable by virtue of modular flow.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhi Jiang, M\'ark Mezei

item.title: Holographic RG Flows from Running Couplings
item.description: arXiv:2406.17221v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the RG flow in the holographic setup and study new IR physics at the IR fixed point, when a relevant scalar operator deforms a two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT). On the dual gravity side, the renormalization group (RG) flow from the UV to the IR CFT can be described by a scalar field rolling from an unstable to a stable equilibrium point. Specifically, to make the scale dependence of the RG flow more explicit, we study the running coupling constant obtained by solving the beta function. After considering a simple scalar potential, we study the change of the coupling constant and its effect on the ground state along the RG flow. We showed that the central charge monotonically decreases along the RG flow, and its value at the IR fixed point is determined by the conformal dimension of the deformation operator and the coupling constant at the IR fixed point. We further investigate how changing the ground state influences the two-point function and conformal dimension of a local operator in the probe limit.
item.dc:creator: Chanyong Park, Jung Hun Lee

item.title: 6d Large Charge and 2d Virasoro Blocks
item.description: arXiv:2409.05944v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute observables in the interacting rank-one 6d $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ SCFT at large R-charge. We focus on correlators involving $\Phi^n$, namely symmetric products of the bottom component of the supermultiplet containing the stress-tensor. By using the moduli space effective action and methods from the large-charge expansion, we compute the OPE coefficients $\langle\Phi^n\Phi^m\Phi^{n+m}\rangle$ in an expansion in 1/n. The coefficients of the expansion are only partially determined from the 6d perspective, but we manage to fix them order-by-order in 1/n numerically by utilizing the 6d/2d correspondence. This is made possible by the fact that this $6d$ observable can be extracted in 2d from a specific double-scaling limit of the vacuum Virasoro block, which can be efficiently computed numerically. We also extend the computation to higher-rank SCFTs, and discuss various applications of our results to 6d as well as 2d.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan J. Heckman, Adar Sharon, Masataka Watanabe

item.title: Comments on Celestial CFT and $AdS_{3}$ String Theory
item.description: arXiv:2410.02620v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a recent work, Ogawa et al. (2024) proposed a model for celestial conformal field theory (CFT) based on the $H_{3}^{+}$-Wess-Zumino-Novikov-Witten (WZNW) model. In this paper, we extend the model advanced by Ogawa et al. (2024), demonstrating how it can holographically generate tree-level MHV scattering amplitudes for both gluons and gravitons when analytically continued to the ultra-hyperbolic Klein space $\mathbf{R}_{2}^{2}$, thereby offering an alternative to celestial Liouville theory. We construct a holographic dictionary in which vertex operators and conformal primaries in celestial CFT are derived from their worldsheet counterparts in Euclidean $AdS_{3}$ (bosonic) string theory. Within this dictionary, we derive the celestial stress-energy tensor, compute the two- and three-point functions, and determine the celestial operator product expansion (OPE). Additionally, we derive a system of partial differential equations that characterises the celestial amplitudes of our model, utilising the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) equations and worldsheet Ward identities. In the Appendix, we provide a concise introduction to the $H_{3}^{+}$-WZNW model, with emphasis on its connection to Euclidean $AdS_{3}$ string theory.
item.dc:creator: Igor Mol

item.title: The entanglement membrane in 2d CFT: reflected entropy, RG flow, and information velocity
item.description: arXiv:2411.16542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The time evolution of entanglement entropy in generic chaotic many-body systems has an effective description in terms of a minimal membrane, characterised by a tension function. For 2d CFTs, a degenerate tension function reproduces several results regarding the dynamics of the entropy; this stands in contrast to higher dimensions where the tension is non-degenerate. In this paper we use holography to show that, in order to correctly capture the reflected entropy in 2d CFT, one needs to add an additional degree of freedom to the membrane description. Furthermore, we show that the conventional non-degenerate membrane tension function emerges upon introducing a relevant deformation of the CFT, dual to a planar BTZ black hole with scalar hair and with an interior Kasner universe. Finally, we also study the membrane description for reflected entropy and information velocity arXiv:1908.06993 in higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhi Jiang, M\'ark Mezei, Julio Virrueta

item.title: Contact diagrams for chords
item.description: arXiv:2503.22619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate how contact chord diagrams can arise from certain Fock-space models and compute the corresponding correlation functions using the chord path integral technique. In particular, our three-point functions are in the right form dictated by conformal symmetry, and some of our four-point functions match the results of some AdS$_2$ contact Witten diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Jia

item.title: Perturbative K\"ahler Moduli Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2506.08083v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we present two classes of inflationary models in the framework of type IIB string theory. The inflatons correspond to blow-up K\"ahler modulus arising from compactifying type IIB string theory on a Calabi-Yau. Using perturbative corrections, we first highlight a procedure for stabilising more than one K\"ahler modulus. For the case of two K\"ahler moduli, we explicitly construct two classes of inflationary potentials within the K\"ahler cone which satisfy both EFT and cosmological constraints. The first class of models, arising from moduli redefinition of the blow-up mode, garners a potential of the form $V(\phi)=V_{0}(1+C_{1} \phi^{2/3})$ align with CMB data with tensor-to-scalar ratio $r\lesssim 10^{-2}$. The second class of models, which have been recently proposed as loop blow-up inflation, have a form $V(\phi)=V_{0}(1+C_{2}\phi^{-2/3})$, also agrees with CMB data with tensor-to-scalar ratio $r\lesssim 10^{-8}$. Our work differs from the original loop blow-up inflation in terms of stabilization mechanism and subsequently the tensor-to-scalar ratio.
item.dc:creator: Mishaal Hai, Ahmed Rakin Kamal, Noshin Ferdous Shamma, Md Shaikot Jahan Shuvo

item.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2509.02239v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.
item.dc:creator: Elia Mazzucchelli, Prashanth Raman

item.title: Time Evolution of Multi-Party Entanglement Signals
item.description: arXiv:2511.16729v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the real-time dynamics of multi-party entanglement signals in chaotic quantum many-body systems including but not necessarily restricted to holographic conformal field theories. We find that scrambling dynamics generates multiparty entanglement with rich structure including: (a) qualitatively different dynamical behaviours for different signals, likely reflecting different dynamics for different kinds of entanglement patterns, (b) discontinuities indicating dynamical phase transitions in the entanglement structure, (c) transient and non-monotonic multiparty entanglement, and (d) periods during which the extensive entanglement of some regions is entirely multipartite. Our main technical tool is the membrane theory of entanglement dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Vijay Balasubramanian, Hanzhi Jiang, Simon F. Ross

item.title: Entanglement in the Schwinger effect
item.description: arXiv:2512.10091v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze entanglement generated by the Schwinger effect using a mode-by-mode formalism for scalar and spinor QED in constant backgrounds. Starting from thermal initial states, we derive compact, closed-form results for bipartite entanglement between particle-antiparticle partners in terms of the Bogoliubov coefficients. For bosons, thermal fluctuations enhance production but suppress quantum correlations: the logarithmic negativity is nonzero only below a (mode-dependent) critical temperature $T_c$. At fixed $T$, entanglement appears only above a critical field $E_{\text{entang}}$. For fermions, we observe a qualitatively different pattern: the fermionic logarithmic negativity is non-vanishing at finite temperature, and is monotonically suppressed by thermal noise. As a function of the electric field, it is non-monotonic, featuring a temperature-independent optimal field strength $E_*$ and decreasing on both sides of the maximum. We give quantitative estimates for analog experiments, where our entanglement criteria convert directly into concrete temperature and electric field constraints. These findings identify realistic regimes where the quantum character of Schwinger physics may be tested in the laboratory.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Kranas, Amaury Marchon, Silvia Pla

item.title: Modular Krylov Complexity as a Boundary Probe of Area Operators and Entanglement Islands
item.description: arXiv:2602.02675v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the area operator of a quantum extremal surface can be reconstructed directly from boundary dynamics without reference to bulk geometry. Our approach combines the operator-algebra quantum error-correction (OAQEC) structure of AdS/CFT with modular Krylov complexity. Using Lanczos coefficients of boundary modular dynamics, we extract the spectrum of the modular Hamiltonian restricted to the algebra of the entanglement wedge and isolate its central contribution, which is identified with the area operator. The construction is purely boundary-based and applies to superpositions of semiclassical geometries as well. As a prospective application, we discuss island formation and the Page transition in evaporating black holes using boundary modular evolution, bypassing any bulk extremization. More broadly, our results establish modular Krylov complexity as a probe of emergent spacetime geometry, providing a new route to accessing black hole interiors from boundary quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Niloofar Vardian

item.title: Nucleating an Inflationary Universe: Euclidean Wormholes and their No-Boundary Limit
item.description: arXiv:2603.11003v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: No-boundary instantons and Euclidean "wineglass" wormholes have both been proposed as providing suitable initial conditions for the current expanding phase of our universe, and in particular for providing conditions that are favorable to an inflationary phase. These finite action solutions have generally been regarded as unrelated, and enacting different scenarios - in one case the creation of spacetime from nothing, and in the other up-tunneling from a Euclidean Anti-de Sitter vacuum. By studying explicit solutions of both axionic and magnetic wineglass wormholes, we find that in the zero-charge limit the throat of the wormholes pinches off, leaving a no-boundary instanton that disconnects from the asymptotic Anti-de Sitter region. Thus wormholes and no-boundary instantons are part of a common family of Euclidean solutions. Along the way, we resolve the long-known puzzle that the action of wineglass wormholes can become negative. Moreover, small-charge wormholes lead to a longer inflationary phase than large-charge solutions, while no-boundary instantons dominate the probability distribution overall.
item.dc:creator: George Lavrelashvili, Jean-Luc Lehners

item.title: Subleading Chern-Simons soft factors in perturbative de Sitter
item.description: arXiv:2605.05130v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chern--Simons perturbations introduce corrections to soft theorems for gauge theories at subleading $\mathcal{O}\left(\omega^0\right)$ order in soft momenta. We investigate these soft theorems in flat spacetime with perturbative $1/\ell^2$ de Sitter corrections. Following previous works, we define the perturbative scattering matrix in a compact region in the static patch of de Sitter. We start with computing the soft theorem for an $n$-gluon amplitude in pure Yang--Mills. We then add a Chern--Simons perturbation and compute the correction to the subleading soft theorem. We show that Chern--Simons corrections do not mix with the $1/\ell^2$ de Sitter curvature corrections at subleading order $\mathcal{O}\left(\omega^0\right)$. Alternatively, one can say that the subleading Chern--Simons soft factors are insensitive to the de Sitter curvature at this order, indicating their topological nature at the level of amplitudes. This also suggests a universal behavior of these Chern--Simons soft factors.
item.dc:creator: Pratik Chattopadhyay, Avi Wadhwa

item.title: Non-Abelian Dirac oscillator in a uniform Yang--Mills background: spin--isospin mixing and singlet--triplet splitting
item.description: arXiv:2605.30403v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a planar Dirac oscillator coupled to a spatially uniform \(\utwo=\uone\times\su\) Yang--Mills background. The gauge configuration, adapted from the Dossa--Avossevou construction, contains an Abelian magnetic field \(B\), a non-Abelian spatial amplitude \(\beta\), and a non-Abelian scalar amplitude \(\rho\). Within the Pauli-reduced formulation, the non-Abelian field strength produces a constant operator on \(\mathbb{C}^{2}_{\mathrm{spin}}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{2}_{\mathrm{iso}}\). This operator contains a diagonal internal-Zeeman contribution proportional to \(\sigma^{3}T^{3}\) and an off-diagonal spin--isospin term proportional to \(\sigma^{1}T^{1}+\sigma^{2}T^{2}\). Its diagonalization gives a doubly degenerate aligned branch and two mixed branches with eigenvalues \[ \lambda_{\mathrm{FM}}=\frac{g^{2}\beta^{2}}{4m},\qquad \lambda_{S}=-\frac{g^{2}\beta(\beta-2\rho)}{4m},\qquad \lambda_{T}=-\frac{g^{2}\beta(\beta+2\rho)}{4m}. \] Consequently, the aligned internal-Zeeman scale is quadratic in \(\beta\), whereas the singlet--triplet separation is linear in \(\beta\rho\). The revised formulation makes the sign conventions explicit, verifies the main limiting cases, distinguishes the Pauli-reduced spectrum from a full first-order Dirac diagonalization, and clarifies the physical meaning of the numerical illustrations.
item.dc:creator: Abdelmalek Boumali

item.title: Flowing with Displacements and Tilts: Surface Operators in $O(N)$ Models
item.description: arXiv:2606.03974v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Defect conformal field theories have special operators of protected dimension known as displacements and tilts. They arise due to the breaking of global symmetries by the defect and the normalisations of their two-point functions are characteristics of the defect. In the case of surface defects, these normalisations are related to some of the anomaly coefficients in the surface effective action. To study these operators and their flows between different defect renormalization group fixed points we present an elegant approach using conformal perturbation theory that easily reproduces the known examples from the critical Wilson-Fisher $O(N)$ model in $4-\varepsilon$ dimensions and allows us to construct new ones in other multiscalar theories. In all the systems that we study the flows are short and under full control, as is the change of the displacement and tilt normalizations. We point out some novel features like the existence of vortices when the defect conformal manifold is not simply connected. In addition to regular human labour, this work relied heavily on generative AI; see full disclosure in methodology section.
item.dc:creator: Jake Belton, Nadav Drukker, Biswajit Sahoo

item.title: Finite N Black Holes through the Brick Wall
item.description: arXiv:2606.06613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In AdS/CFT at finite $N$, black holes are described by ordinary quantum systems with finite entropy and discrete spectra, while semiclassical bulk effective field theory treats the near-horizon region as an ideal continuum. We reconsider the brick-wall model as a simple effective description of the finite $N$ departure from the semiclassical near-horizon continuum in AdS/CFT. A Dirichlet wall is reflecting; however, once the regulated near-wall modes are replaced by interacting stretched-horizon degrees of freedom, the exterior simple sector can look absorptive and black-hole-like. If these degrees of freedom are thermally populated while the exterior incoming modes are in their vacuum, they radiate as ordinary hot matter, and this gives Hawking radiation. Furthermore, we show that finite $N$ prevents the near-horizon sector from being an ideal continuum absorber; the brick-wall model is a simple effective representation of this limitation, where the failure of perfect absorption appears as residual reflection or echoes. Such return effects appear on the echo time scale $\kappa^{-1}\log S_{\rm BH}$ and are not expected to be suppressed as $e^{-S_{\rm BH}}$, although their detailed amplitude is model-dependent. We also discuss brick-wall-like models in which the effective inner boundary arises dynamically from a regular matter core rather than from an imposed boundary condition.
item.dc:creator: Seiji Terashima

item.title: Asymptotic Algebras and Holography of Information in CGHS Model
item.description: arXiv:2606.09346v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Holography of Information (HoI) and the island formula are two recent approaches to the black hole information loss paradox that yield different Page curves. The difference between the Page curves has been argued to be rooted in the algebra that each approach focuses on. In this paper, we study the candidate algebras for the CGHS model. For the gravitational completion constructed here and under assumptions analogous to those made in previous HoI literature, we establish HoI for the CGHS model coupled to a massless scalar by constructing the radiative phase space and asymptotic algebras at future null infinity. We prove that the quantum state of the right-moving modes can be recovered from an arbitrarily small neighbourhood of the past endpoint of the right future null infinity. We then argue that island reconstruction is incompatible with exact commutativity of the left and right radiative algebras. We discuss the possible distinction between the HoI and island approaches for the CGHS model.
item.dc:creator: Waheed A. Dar, Nirmalya Kajuri, Rinkesh Panigrahi

item.title: Quantum States Prepared by Wormholes: Long-Wavelength Deviations from Bunch-Davies
item.description: arXiv:2607.12772v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wineglass wormholes mediate the nucleation of baby universes out of an asymptotically Anti-de Sitter or flat spacetime. Upon materialization, the new universe naturally undergoes an inflationary phase. Here we study the quantum state of tensor and probe scalar field fluctuations that these wormhole geometries prepare, finding that they reproduce the Bunch-Davies vacuum for short-wavelength modes but lead to deviations from Bunch-Davies on large scales. These deviations, which depend on the charge of the wormhole, cause a small shift as well as oscillations in the angular power spectrum generated by an ensuing inflationary phase, and thus provide a distinctive cosmological observable. The wormholes are supported by either axionic or magnetic charges. In the limit of vanishing charge, they undergo a topological transition after which they contain no-boundary instantons. We find that the small-charge limit suppresses deviations from the Bunch-Davies state for both scalar and tensor fluctuations, indicating that the topological transition is smooth.
item.dc:creator: George Lavrelashvili, Jean-Luc Lehners

item.title: Emergence of Lorentzian geometry from string Carroll geometry
item.description: arXiv:2607.23760v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The near horizon region of a generic non extremal black hole has been extensively studied in terms of a Carrollian geometry with two null directions, also called a string Carroll geometry. We investigate how this string Carroll geometry evolves to a Lorentzian throat as the four dimensional Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN) black hole approaches extremality. We identify the quadratic temporal contribution that is suppressed in the non extremal description but is required to recover the $\mathrm{AdS}_2$ curvature. Approaching the outer horizon and extremality simultaneously, scaling the horizon separation together with the radial distance and correspondingly rescaling Killing time, brings this contribution into the leading longitudinal metric alongside the Rindler sector. In ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, the string Carroll metric alone has a Lorentzian limit with a flat longitudinal sector. The quadratic temporal term arises from the bilinear of the leading and subleading longitudinal coframe fields and supplies the missing curvature, while higher radial contributions vanish. The reconstructed limiting geometry is already locally $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times S^2$ at finite positive scaled horizon separation; setting this parameter to zero makes the selected horizon extremal without changing the local curvature. The limiting metric and Maxwell field satisfy the Einstein-Maxwell equations. In static coordinates, the temporal component again follows from the quadratic term, while the radial component requires summing contributions from all radial orders. The reconstruction provides a geometric starting point for investigating which expansion data must be retained when extending calculations based on the non extremal string Carroll description into the throat regime, including their implications for string, particle and field dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Anirudhda Shinde, Mangesh Mandlik

item.title: R7-branes and AdS$_{\text{9}}$ solutions in type IIB
item.description: arXiv:2608.07664v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the recently found $\mathrm{AdS}_9$ backgrounds in type IIB supergravity. We start by reviewing the solutions in a more convenient set of coordinates, which allows us to explicitly compute a few relevant observables, including the holographic central charge. Subsequently, we study non-supersymmetric 7-brane configurations sourced by the IIB axio-dilaton. We find explicit analytic 7-brane solutions that possess the above $\mathrm{AdS}_9$ backgrounds as their near-horizon geometry. Finally, we discuss the relation of these 7-brane solutions to the R7 branes by imposing the reflection monodromy $\tau \rightarrow -\bar \tau$ in the transverse plane.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Dibitetto, Cameron Gibson, Nicol\`o Petri, Colin Sterckx

item.title: Gravitational Faraday rotation, gravitational spin Hall effect, and spin-refined causality analysis from Magnusian matrix in effective field theories of gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.10871v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The effects of black hole's spin in effective field theories (EFTs) of gravity are explored through observables of wave scattering on black hole backgrounds in the geometric optics approximation. The considered observables are polarisation rotation angle, wavenumber kick (or deflection angle), and (Shapiro/Wigner--Smith) time delay, each of which are related to gravitational Faraday rotation, gravitational spin Hall effect, and infrared causality. The observables are computed from scattering amplitudes through the Magnusian formalism, where the Magnusian is promoted to a matrix to account for helicity information. It is found that (1) the gravitational spin Hall effect in EFTs of gravity are qualitatively different from that of general relativity due to "noncommutative" wavenumber kicks, and (2) black hole's spin slightly enhances the causality constraints on EFT coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Kibok Jeong, Jung-Wook Kim, Soochang Lee

item.title: D4-branes wrapped on topological disks from matter-coupled F(4) gauged supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.12850v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a number of supersymmetric $AdS_4\times \Sigma$ solutions with $\Sigma$ being a topological disk with non-trivial $U(1)$ holonomy on the boundary or a ``half-spindle'' from matter-coupled $F(4)$ gauged supergravity. The gauged supergravity is coupled to three vector multiplets with $SO(3)\times SO(3)$ gauge group. The resulting solutions preserve eight supercharges and $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ or $SO(2)_{\text{diag}}$ symmetries and are expected to be dual to $N=2$ SCFTs in three dimensions arising from compactifications of five-dimensional $N=2$ SCFT on a half-spindle. All of the solutions lie within the $U(1)\times U(1)$ subsector of the matter-coupled $F(4)$ gauged supergravity that can be embedded in massive type IIA theory. After uplifted to ten dimensions, the solutions can be interpreted as a system of D4-D8-branes wrapped on $\Sigma$. Some of the solutions are asymptotic to a locally $AdS_6$ geometry and can be identified as codimension-2 conformal defects within the $N=2$ SCFT in five dimensions. For these solutions, the circle inside $\Sigma$ decompactifies in the $AdS_6$ limit rendering the holographic free energy infinite. There also exist solutions with finite free energy in the dual three-dimensional SCFTs. In addition, we show that the results both extend the previously known solutions and provide a novel class of solutions.
item.dc:creator: Patharadanai Nuchino, Parinya Karndumri

item.title: Who Writes the Gravitational Second Law of Thermodynamics?
item.description: arXiv:2608.16997v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define gravitational entropy as the manifestly integrable surface charge associated with local transverse Lorentz boosts, entirely bypassing the conventional reliance on spacetime diffeomorphisms. Any notion of entropy must satisfy the second law. To answer the question posed in the title, an analogy with Newtonian classical mechanics is instructive: Newton's second law of motion is written by inertial observers who are defined by the first law of mechanics. We show that the second law of gravitational thermodynamics is written by free-fall observers with path parameterization in which the non-affinity of the geodesics is equal to the expansion of their velocity vector field. We then provide a proof of the local second law by studying variations in entropy as viewed by this class of covariantly-defined causal free-fall observers. We show that the entropy variation is strictly non-decreasing, provided the matter sector satisfies the integrated strong energy condition along the observer path.
item.dc:creator: V. R. Shajiee, M. M. Sheikh-Jabbari, V. Taghiloo

item.title: The large $N$ vector model with angular velocity
item.description: arXiv:2608.31151v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the free energy of a critical vector model at large $N$ on $S^{1}\times S^{2}$ with an angular velocity $\hat\mu$ without the singlet constraint. We study the model for which the large $N$ dynamics is controlled by the uniform saddle point of the auxiliary field arising in the Hubbard-Stratanovich transformation. The leading high-temperature behaviour is determined analytically both as an expansion about $\hat\mu r=0$ and $\hat\mu^{2}r^{2}=1$ where $r$ is the radius of the sphere. We supplement the analytic results with a numerical analysis that agrees with both the analytical expansions in their respective regimes and smoothly interpolates between them. The leading high-temperature contribution to the free energy develops a pole at $\hat\mu^{2}r^{2}=1$, in agreement with expectations from the thermal effective field theory. Its residue coincides with that of the massless free theory. Sub-leading terms, however, exhibit non-analytic dependence on the angular velocity and distinguish the critical fixed-point result from the free theory answer. The residue at the pole can also be obtained by placing the model on the pp-wave geometry. We show that the residue agrees with that obtained from the direct computation. The free energy of the model connects the non-trivial fixed point of the $O(N)$ model at $\hat\mu r=0$ to its free fixed point at $\hat\mu^2r^2=1$.
item.dc:creator: Justin R. David, Srijan Kumar

item.title: Matrix Holography on an Optical Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2609.05613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an analog quantum-simulation protocol based on a lattice of atomic ensembles and time-averaged Floquet dynamics to construct the four-body potentials that typically appear in bosonic BFSS-like matrix quantum mechanics. In contrast to gate-based digital implementations requiring deep circuits, our approach generates the target model through a fixed set of control stages per Floquet cycle, keeping the number of consecutive unitaries constant with respect to the matrix size $N$. The principal scaling cost in our construction is given by the frequency range required to control the growing lattice. We show that this cost grows at most as $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$, giving a polynomial scaling route to large$-N$, attractive to experimental implementation. Additionally, we demonstrate that the coupling parameter can be tuned beyond $\mathcal{O}(1)$, enabling the simulation of strong-coupling physics necessary for holographic phases.
item.dc:creator: Robin L\"owenberg, Julian Sonner

item.title: Quantum Tunneling from Perturbation Theory Revisited
item.description: arXiv:2609.10134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the late 1990s, Suzuki and Yasuta proposed a compact formula that extracts the decay rate per unit volume of a false vacuum in the $D$-dimensional $O(N)$ $\lambda(\phi^2)^2$ theory with an unbounded potential from conventional perturbative coefficients of the vacuum energy density, i.e.\ vacuum bubble diagrams. The idea was to identify the imaginary part arising from the Borel integral along the discontinuity of the Borel transform with that of the vacuum energy density. While the formula works quite well for~$D=1$, i.e.\ quantum mechanics, its validity remained unclear for~$D\geq2$ because only the first three perturbative coefficients for~$D=2$ were available and the result showed no sign of convergence. In the present paper, we reexamine this approach using the first seven nontrivial perturbative coefficients (up to nine loops) for~$D=2$ and~$N=1$ obtained by Serone, Spada, and~Villadoro. Introducing two tunable parameters in the finite-order truncated Borel transform following these authors, we find that the imaginary part converges as the perturbative order increases, with the last few orders agreeing to within a few percent. In the intermediate range of the coupling constant, $3\lesssim\widetilde{g}\lesssim8$, this approach yields an imaginary part rather close to the leading-order semiclassical approximation with the one-loop determinant; it is $10$--$20\%$ larger than the semiclassical result with the two-loop correction computed by Malatesta, Parisi, and~Rizzo. Our result is consistent, within errors, with the continuum extrapolation of the Pad\'e-resummed linked-cluster expansion in a quantum $\phi^4$ chain.
item.dc:creator: Hiroshi Suzuki

item.title: Learning Scattering Amplitudes with Transformer Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2609.32096v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a transformer reinforcement learning algorithm that learns to solve high loop-level scattering amplitudes in planar N = 4 Super Yang-Mills theory. Our algorithm improves on previous transformer-only results by incorporating previously derived symmetries and relationships into the learning algorithm. This results in a greatly decreased fraction of the solution that needs to be known a priori to solve the entire problem. An additional benefit is that our algorithm also ensures that every output obeys the set of known relationships. Rather than predicting all coefficients independently, the model proposes assignments that are propagated through exact linear relations, while MCTS searches over assignments when propagation alone is insufficient. This is crucial to the generalization of machine learning approaches to higher loops, as without this, there is no way to overcome the factorially scaling of state sizes and compare to results derived via other methods. Using the symbology representation of the form factor, we frame the problem as learning a mapping between discrete sequences and integer coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Philip Velie, Piyush Jha, Vijay Ganesh, Aishik Ghosh

item.title: Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations and the analytic structure of strings in AdS$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2609.35495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The pole structure of string correlators in AdS$_3$ encodes essential information about the AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ duality. The corresponding residues for spectrally flowed three-point functions have been extracted from their exact expressions and shown to match the predictions of the holographic CFT. Away from the tensionless point, the latter is defined perturbatively in terms of a deformed symmetric orbifold. For $n$-point functions, such a matching has so far only been achieved for a specific subset of poles, and only by means of free-field techniques. Here we develop an alternative approach. We show that, starting from the localization properties of worldsheet correlators, one can solve the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) equations on the corresponding locus and perform the integration over worldsheet moduli explicitly for any $n$ and for arbitrary values of the spectral flow charges. In this way we reproduce, directly from the exact worldsheet theory and including the normalization, the residues previously obtained with free-field methods. We expect this to provide a systematic framework for computing the remaining residues and, ultimately, for determining the full analytic structure of string amplitudes in AdS$_3$.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Iguri, Nicolas Kovensky, Julian H. Toro

item.title: Fast holographic inversion of superconducting domes
item.description: arXiv:2610.09938v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A holographic superconductor whose scalar mass depends on the gauge field strength, $M(\Fsq)$, reproduces a superconducting dome for a suitable $M$, but recovering $M$ from a dome has taken days. We obtain the condition that fixes the critical temperature from two integrations, started at the horizon and at the boundary, and its derivative with respect to $M$ from the same two solutions, so training needs no finite differences and an inversion takes ten minutes to an hour. With this speed we study the interval between the horizon value of $\Fsq$ at the lowest doping and $\Fsq=0$, which no horizon reaches and at whose end the scalar mass $M(0)$ fixes the dimension of the dual operator. Holding $M(0)$ at several values, the pinned masses, and retraining the rest, we find reconstructions that share the minima of $M$ and agree wherever the horizons reach, apart from the deepest end, but differ on that interval. A rule that keeps the reconstruction with the simplest closed form recovers the scalar mass and the mass function of a dome generated from a quadratic $M$. On Gaussian and double-Gaussian domes and the measured phase diagrams of YBa$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{y}$ and 2M-WS$_{2}$ its choice rests on ties or narrow margins, and it recovers the scalar mass of only two of the four domes generated from the closed forms it keeps for them. The dome thus constrains $M$ where its horizons reach but not the scalar mass, which a second observable would have to fix.
item.dc:creator: Sejin Kim

item.title: Love at First Loop: Quantum Deformability of Near-Extremal Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17259v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The static Love numbers of black holes vanish in classical, four-dimensional, asymptotically flat General Relativity. We study how this changes for the response of near-extremal Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes to a minimally coupled massless scalar, at energies where the Schwarzian mode of the near-horizon throat fluctuates strongly. The black hole then responds as a quantum system with a spectrum of states. Its static response is a polarizability, given by virtual transitions between them. For $\ell=0$ the static Love number vanishes, by the shift symmetry of the scalar, but for multipoles $\ell\geq1$ the static Love numbers are nonzero: the finite rotational energy of the spin-$\ell$ intermediate states spoils the cancellation responsible for the classical result. Since the throat no longer has a classical geometry from which to read off a tidal response, we define it through the retarded Green's function, and compute its full frequency dependence at leading order in $r_+\omega$. Its conservative part requires renormalization: the near-horizon theory fixes the coefficient of its logarithm, and with it a dependence on the energy that no local term can remove, while its finite local terms are matching data of the four-dimensional theory. The dissipative part is finite and scheme independent. For $\ell\geq1$, it vanishes at low frequencies when the energy is below the rotational gap, while at the gap threshold it becomes non-analytic in frequency and produces a late-time $t^{-3/2}$ tail.
item.dc:creator: Pablo A. Cano, Marina David, Roberto Emparan, Stefano Trezzi

item.title: Compensator-free $\mathcal N=2$ extension of ModMax and scalar propagation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23447v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a compensator-free $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal and electric--magnetic duality-invariant extension of ModMax electrodynamics in ordinary flat superspace. The action is built entirely from the Abelian vector multiplet, using a derivative composite of its field strength, and the self-duality equation is solved to all orders as a formal series in the coupling. Upon setting the additional $\mathcal N=1$ chiral multiplet to zero, the action is equivalent off shell to the $\mathcal N=1$ ModMax action of Bandos, Lechner, Sorokin and Townsend through a local vector-prepotential redefinition. Since the complex scalar of the $\mathcal N=2$ multiplet is set to zero in this reduction, we add one superconformal interaction that leaves the reduction unchanged and is chosen to ensure causal scalar propagation. On constant non-null electromagnetic backgrounds with vanishing scalar expectation value, the higher-order scalar coefficients are fixed by requiring the scalar quadratic action to satisfy the stress-tensor square-root flow, modulo equations of motion and a total derivative. We determine the quadratic action of the full multiplet on these backgrounds to all orders. Its analytic continuation to finite $\gamma\geq0$ gives causal scalar propagation, with transverse speed squared $e^{-\gamma}$ and unit longitudinal speed, the ModMax photon cones, luminal gauginos with positive kinetic coefficients, and auxiliary fields with algebraic equations of motion.
item.dc:creator: Ariunzul Davgadorj

item.title: On 2-loop AdS$_2$ superstring partition function in AdS$_5 \times S^5$ and AdS$_4\times CP^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.37096v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit the 2-loop computation of the partition function of the GS superstring expanded near the AdS$_2$ surface in AdS$_5\times S^5$ and AdS$_4\times {\rm CP}^3$, dual to $\frac{1}{2}$ BPS circular Wilson loop in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM and ABJM theories. In arXiv:2601.08809 it was done in AdS$_5\times S^5$ using dimensional regularization and a UV pole was found. Since dimensional regularization is problematic for the GS string, here we use a heat-kernel cutoff instead. Then the contribution of the local path integral measure, proportional to $\delta(0)$, can no longer be ignored. We show that it cancels the $\delta(0)$ terms coming from the quartic interactions in the action, leaving the square of the difference ${\rm Str}\,E$ between the regularized numbers of bosonic and fermionic modes. The result is thus UV finite, the pole of arXiv:2601.08809 being an artefact of dimensional regularization. If all fields are regularized with the same smearing kernel, ${\rm Str}\,E=0$ and the 2-loop coefficient $f_2$ vanishes, in tension with $f_2=\frac{3}{32\pi^2}$ in SYM theory. In the AdS$_4\times{\rm CP}^3$ case the same cancellation leaves a finite term proportional to the square of the coincident value of the massless 2d fermion Green's function, giving, ironically, $f_2=\frac{3}{32\pi^2}$ instead of $f_2=0$ required by localization. This term is the level-zero (string) part of the result of arXiv:2609.14497 for the AdS$_2\times S^1$ M2 brane in AdS$_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, where it is cancelled by the higher $S^1$ modes, which also remove a finite mass shift of the massless fermion in conflict with the AdS$_2$ supersymmetry. This suggests that the type II string path integral measure should contain an extra contribution, supplied in the IIA case by the parent M2 brane; in the AdS$_5\times S^5$ case it is still to be identified and may resolve the remaining 2-loop mismatch with localization.
item.dc:creator: Arkady A. Tseytlin

item.title: MPS overlaps and Sklyanin determinants
item.description: arXiv:2610.37285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive explicit overlap functions for integrable matrix product states associated with arbitrary finite-dimensional irreducible evaluation representations of the orthogonal and symplectic twisted Yangians. The central step is to relate the commuting quasi-determinants entering the universal overlap formula to Sklyanin determinants of nested subalgebras. For orthogonal evaluation representations, this relation determines their spectra directly in the Gelfand--Tsetlin basis. In the symplectic case, we combine Sklyanin determinants and minors with a factorization of the nested rank-two boundary matrices to obtain the corresponding spectra. The resulting overlap functions are explicit products parametrized by Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns and require only the highest-weight data of the underlying orthogonal or symplectic representation. Together with the universal ratio of Gaudin determinants and the model-dependent pseudovacuum overlap coefficients, they determine the normalized MPS overlaps. We also express the overlap functions in the orthogonal case beyond evaluation representations in terms of the highest weights arising along the nested twisted-Yangian subalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Tamas Gombor

item.title: Entanglement Bounds on Cardy Growth in Higher Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.37449v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose bounds relating thermal entropy to entanglement in unitary conformal field theories: $f\le4\pi^2a$ in four dimensions and $f\le2.99830949\ldots\,F$ in three dimensions. Here $f$ is the dimensionless coefficient of the cosmological constant term in the thermal effective action, $a$ is the Euler anomaly coefficient, and $F$ is the sphere free energy. These bounds arise naturally as the high-temperature limits of proposed inequalities for spherical R\'enyi entropy that extend the conformal collider bound in four dimensions and an analogous conjecture in three dimensions. To verify this proposal, we formulate a stronger conjectural inequality common to both dimensions, expressed in terms of the stress-tensor three-point function and saturated by every free theory. We establish this inequality in controlled regimes of weakly coupled gauge theories, large-$N$ vector models, and holographic CFTs. Finite-$N$ numerical results provide additional support. Our proposal suggests that the equality between the universal coefficients governing the Cardy formula and entanglement entropy in two-dimensional CFTs extends to higher dimensions in the form of a universal inequality.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Kusuki, Yin Tang

item.title: Reflected constraint algebras of open Carroll--Weyl null strings
item.description: arXiv:2610.37546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study whether open null strings admit the full Carroll--Weyl gauge symmetry consistently with endpoint conditions and nontrivial physical degrees of freedom. For endpoints constrained to timelike defects, natural variations imply that any nonzero Carroll flow must be tangent to the worldsheet boundary. For a fixed linear defect through the target origin, we construct a differentiable Hamiltonian system on this branch. Its complete Carroll--Weyl generator requires no additional boundary charge. Smooth reflection defines a preserved subdomain and gives a circle interpretation to selected sine and cosine modes of the constraints. Their centreless algebra extends the two-constraint open-string algebra by the local scale constraint. An endpoint obstruction shows that this reflection condition excludes some gauge orbits of the natural interval theory: we exhibit a regular four-dimensional solution with no corresponding reflected representative. Within the reflected sector, we construct a local canonical field pair and conserved target-space Lorentz charges. A separate solution family has nonzero boost charge and a nondegenerate two-dimensional symplectic pullback. The constraint algebra, the boundary choice, and the physical observables thus provide complementary information about the open theory.
item.dc:creator: Limin Zeng

item.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and R\'enyi entropies
item.description: arXiv:2610.40371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$, in the probe limit, is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. When the scalar mass saturates the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling takes the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase can be found in closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is linearly stable, as is any nodeless probe-limit condensate in the standard quantization with a nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On each slicing it answers a different question about the dual conformal field theory. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and the attenuation of sound are found in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it describes a state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$, arguably the lowest-energy one, and gives its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers that the superfluid effective theory does not describe; they come from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector. The hyperbolic slicing gives in closed form a homogeneous hairy phase of the black holes that compute the charged R\'enyi entropies of a ball. Its condensate does not vanish at the entangling surface. When sourced by operators inserted there, the phase sets in at R\'enyi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar.
item.dc:creator: Siqing Yu

item.title: Gauge-invariant quantum gravitational corrections to correlation functions
item.description: arXiv:1710.00839v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A recent proposal for gauge-invariant observables in inflation [R. Brunetti et al., JHEP 1608 (2016) 032] is examined. We give a generalisation of their construction to general background spacetimes. In flat space, we calculate one-loop graviton corrections to a scalar two-point function in a general gauge for the graviton. We explicitely show how the gauge-dependent terms cancel between the usual self-energy contributions and the additional corrections inherent in these observables. The one-loop corrections have the expected functional form, contrary to another recently studied proposal for gauge-invariant observables [M. B. Fr\"ob, Class. Quant. Grav. 35 (2018) 035005] where this is not the case. Furthermore, we determine the one-loop graviton corrections to the four-point coupling of the gauge-invariant scalar field, and the corresponding running of the coupling constant induced by graviton loops. Interestingly, the $\beta$ function is negative for most values of the non-minimal coupling of the scalar field to curvature, including minimal and conformal coupling.
item.dc:creator: Markus B. Fr\"ob

item.title: A Tribute to S. Deser: Conserved Quantities in Generic Gravity Theories
item.description: arXiv:2307.12758v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: I describe parts of my joint work with S. Deser [March 19, 1931 - April 21, 2023] which started when I was working as a post-doc at Brandeis University in 2001. Our work was mostly, but not exclusively, on conserved charges of higher curvature theories of gravity. I also describe some recent developments, such as expressing the conserved charges in terms of the linearized Riemann tensor; I expound upon the computations. I also reminisce about our interaction for over two decades that went beyond our scientific collaboration. The physics part of this review is intended for graduate students and researchers interested in extended theories of gravity, especially about the conserved quantities and perturbative techniques in these theories.
item.dc:creator: Bayram Tekin

item.title: Building blocks for $W$-algebras of classical types
item.description: arXiv:2409.03465v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,3,4,\dots)$ serves as a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,3,\dots,N)$ for some $N$ in the sense that under mild hypothesis, all such vertex algebras arise as quotients of $W_{\infty}$. There is an $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ family of such $1$-parameter vertex algebras which, after tensoring with a Heisenberg algebra, are known as $Y$-algebras. They were introduced by Gaiotto and Rap\v{c}\'ak and are expected to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras in type $A$, i.e., every $W$-(super) algebra in type $A$ is an extension of a tensor product of finitely many $Y$-algebras. Similarly, the orthosymplectic $Y$-algebras are $1$-parameter quotients of a universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,4,6,\dots)$, which is a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,4,\dots, 2N)$ for some $N$. Unlike type $A$, these algebras are not all the building blocks for $W$-algebras of types $B$, $C$, and $D$. In this paper, we construct a new universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra of type $W(1^3, 2, 3^3, 4, 5^3,6,\dots)$ which we denote by $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ since it contains a copy of the affine vertex algebra $V^k(\mathfrak{sp}_2)$. We identify $8$ infinite families of $1$-parameter quotients of $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ which are analogues of the $Y$-algebras. We regard $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ as a fundamental object on equal footing with $W_{\infty}$ and $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$, and we give some heuristic reasons for why we expect the $1$-parameter quotients of these three objects to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras of classical types. Finally, we prove that $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ has many quotients which are strongly rational. This yields new examples of strongly rational $W$-superalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Creutzig, Volodymyr Kovalchuk, Andrew R. Linshaw

item.title: Symplectic Pauli-Schr\"odinger Equation for the Quark-Antiquark Interaction System
item.description: arXiv:2507.20045v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the quantum behavior of a quark-antiquark bound system under the influence of a magnetic field within the symplectic formulation of quantum mechanics. Employing a perturbative approach, we obtain the ground and first excited states of the system described by the Cornell potential, which incorporates both confining and non-confining interactions. After performing a Levi-Civita mapping in phase space, we solve the time-independent symplectic Pauli-Schr\"odinger-type equation and determine the corresponding Wigner function. Special attention is given to the observation of the confinement of the quark-antiquark, that is revealed in the phase space structure. Due to the presence of spin in the Hamiltonian, the results reveal that the magnetic field enhances the non-classicality of the Wigner function, signaling stronger quantum interference and a departure from classical behavior. The experimental mass spectra is used to estimate the intensity of the external field, leading to a value that is in order of the transiet magnetic field measured in non-central heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and LHC.
item.dc:creator: R. R. Luz, R. A. S. Paiva, G. X. A. Petronilo, A. E. Santana, T. M. Rocha Filho, R. G. G. Amorim

item.title: Emergent Gauge Flux in Mixed QED$_3$ with Flavor Chemical Potential: Implications for Magnetized U(1) Dirac Spin Liquids
item.description: arXiv:2508.08528v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We design a lattice model of a "mixed" U(1) gauge field coupled to fermions with a flavor chemical potential and solve it with large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
